name: red-new-session-calendar-ist
note: G1 design §9, item 5 -- G1's acceptance test, one half of a pair. These seven bars straddle IST midnight (18:30 UTC) TWICE over, so IST and UTC cut them into sessions at different bar indices. Under IST (NSE): bars 0-1 are 07-26 (21:30, 22:30 IST) and bars 2-6 are 07-27 (00:30 through 07:30 IST), so the boundary sits after bar 1. The twin fixture red-new-session-calendar-utc.json carries byte-identical bars under a CRYPTO instrument and expects DIFFERENT geometry; a harness test asserts the bars really are identical and the expectations really do differ, so the pair cannot be silently reconciled. Nothing about this is expressible in the IR: the calendar is resolved from the instrument at execution (G7), which is what lets the same saved indicator bound to IST days on NIFTY and UTC days on a crypto chart with no re-save.
source:
indicator("H", shorttitle="H", overlay=true)
newday = na(dayofmonth[1]) or dayofmonth != dayofmonth[1]
plotlevel(newday, close, "SR", extend=extend.until, terminate=terminate.new_session)
